findings.fact: The club development route supports the nine-trick objective with appropriate conditional counting.
findings.explanation: Authorized holdings are South CAK864 opposite North CQ72, with DA/K, HA/K and SA providing five outside winners. Cashing CA, CK and CQ yields five club tricks on 3–2 or four after conceding a trick on 4–1. Heart entries connect the hands, and D3 legally follows West’s DQ.
quotes: Four club tricks suffice for the contract; a 3–2 club break provides five.
Cash the club ace and king, then lead a low club to dummy’s queen.

findings.fact: DK wins the opening trick and preserves the planned controls.
findings.explanation: The authorized trick is DQ–D3–D4 with South holding DAK. DK wins legally, retains DA and leaves CAK864 opposite CQ72 available for the retained club development route.
quotes: Win with the king and develop clubs immediately, retaining the diamond ace and other outside controls for re-entry.

findings.fact: CA starts the feasible club route with the outside entries preserved.
findings.explanation: South has won DK and retains CAK864, DA, HA and SA; North holds CQ72 and HK74. Four club tricks plus the five original outside winners make nine, while a 3–2 break supplies ten total tricks.
quotes: Start establishing clubs while all outside controls remain intact. Four club tricks suffice, and a 3–2 break yields an overtrick.

findings.fact: C2 preserves CQ for the planned third-round winner.
findings.explanation: The authorized current trick is South CA followed by West C3. North holds CQ72, so C2 legally follows while retaining C7 to follow CK and CQ to win the third club round.
quotes: Follow low, preserving the queen to win the third club round as planned.

findings.fact: Both defenders following excludes 5–0 and supports continuing clubs.
findings.explanation: Authorized history records West C3 and East C5 under CA. South retains CK864 opposite CQ7. CK followed by a club to CQ produces at least four total club tricks, with one concession if the original split was 4–1 and outside entries available.
quotes: Both defenders followed to the ace, ruling out a 5–0 break. Continue with the king, then lead to the queen; clubs will supply at least four tricks.

findings.fact: C7 preserves the third-round club entry.
findings.explanation: South’s CK is winning the authorized trick over West C9. North holds CQ7; following C7 leaves CQ available for South’s next club lead from C864, consistent with the retained route.
quotes: Preserve the queen to win the next club round, keeping the planned entry and club establishment intact.

findings.fact: The observed club plays establish 3–2 and make the stated continuation executable.
findings.explanation: Authorized history shows both defenders following to CA and CK, accounting for four of their five clubs. South can lead C4 from C864 to North’s CQ, then regain South through HA while retaining C86 as winners.
quotes: Both defenders followed twice, establishing a 3–2 club break. Lead to the queen to draw the last club, then return via the heart ace to cash the remaining clubs.

findings.fact: H4 reaches the established clubs and preserves ten total tricks.
findings.explanation: Authorized history accounts for all five opposing clubs. North holds HK74 and South HA63, C86, DA and SA, with four tricks already won. H4 to HA, two clubs, DA, SA and a heart to HK provide six further winners.
quotes: All opposing clubs are gone. Lead toward the heart ace to reach South’s two established clubs; the outside winners bring the total to ten tricks.

findings.fact: HA wins the current trick and provides access to the remaining winners.
findings.explanation: The authorized trick is North H4–East H8, and South holds HA63. HA cannot be beaten; South’s C86, DA and SA plus North’s reachable HK supply the remaining winners for ten total tricks.
quotes: Win with the ace to reach the established clubs. Cashing those and the remaining outside winners secures ten tricks.

findings.fact: C8 cashes an established winner while preserving access to HK.
findings.explanation: Authorized history shows all opposing clubs exhausted and five declarer tricks won. South holds C86, DA, SA and H63; North holds HK7 and D865. Discarding low diamonds on the clubs preserves the heart entry, yielding ten total tricks.
quotes: Cash the established clubs, discarding low diamonds from dummy while preserving the heart king. Ten tricks remain assured.

findings.fact: D5 is a legal discard that preserves the remaining winners.
findings.explanation: North is void in clubs and holds D865, HK7 and S862 while South’s established C8 is winning. D5 preserves HK and South’s available heart route to it, consistent with cashing clubs before the outside winners.
quotes: Discard a low diamond, preserving the heart king and both major-suit holdings while South cashes clubs.

findings.fact: The last club and three outside winners provide ten total tricks.
findings.explanation: Authorized facts show six tricks won, South holding C6, DA, SA and H63, and North holding HK7. C6 is established; DA and SA can be cashed before a low heart reaches HK, supplying four further tricks.
quotes: Cash the last club, discarding another low diamond from dummy. The diamond ace, spade ace and heart king then secure ten tricks.

findings.fact: D6 preserves the heart winner and does not obstruct the remaining cashing route.
findings.explanation: North holds D86, HK7 and S862 and is void in clubs on South’s winning C6. Discarding D6 leaves D8 to follow DA and retains HK, reachable from South’s H63 after DA and SA are cashed.
quotes: Discard the low diamond, retaining the heart king and a diamond to follow under South’s ace. Ten tricks remain secure.

findings.fact: The stated order cashes all three remaining winners without stranding one.
findings.explanation: Authorized facts show seven tricks won, South holding DA, SA and H63, and North holding D8, S862 and HK7. DA and SA retain the lead in South, after which a low heart reaches HK for the tenth trick.
quotes: Cash the diamond ace now, then the spade ace before crossing to the heart king, securing ten tricks without blocking any winner.

findings.fact: SA makes the contract and the heart entry supplies an overtrick.
findings.explanation: Eight tricks are already won. South holds SA94 and H63 opposite North S862 and HK7; SA is the ninth winner and a subsequent low heart to HK is the tenth.
quotes: Cash the spade ace for the ninth trick, then lead a heart to dummy’s king for the overtrick.

findings.fact: S2 follows legally while preserving the tenth winner.
findings.explanation: The authorized current trick is South SA–West SJ. North holds S862 and HK7, so S2 follows under the unbeatable ace while leaving HK reachable from South’s H63.
quotes: Follow low under the ace. The heart king remains available for the tenth trick.

findings.fact: H3 leads directly to the established tenth winner.
findings.explanation: Authorized history shows HA already cashed and nine tricks won. South holds H63 opposite North HK7, so H3 legally leads toward HK, which no remaining heart can beat.
quotes: Lead to dummy’s heart king to secure the tenth trick and an overtrick.

findings.fact: HK wins the current trick for the tenth declarer trick.
findings.explanation: The authorized current trick is South H3–West HT, North holds HK7, and HA was previously played. HK therefore wins regardless of East’s remaining heart.
quotes: Win with the king to secure the tenth trick and the overtrick.

findings.fact: The spade play is feasible and further gains are correctly treated as conditional.
findings.explanation: Authorized facts show ten tricks already won, North holding S86 and H7 opposite South S94 and H6. Leading S6 toward S9 is legal. SK, SQ, ST and HQ remain unplayed, so the answer appropriately promises no additional winner.
quotes: Lead a low spade toward South’s nine, playing the nine if East plays low.
Ten tricks are secure; any further trick depends on the defenders’ remaining holdings and play.

findings.fact: S4 concedes to a higher card while retaining S9 conditionally.
findings.explanation: The authorized trick is North S6–East ST and South holds S94. Neither South spade beats ST; S4 legally follows and preserves the higher spot. The retained plan’s instruction to play S9 only if East plays low does not apply to ST.
quotes: The ten beats both spades, so play low and retain the nine as a possible later winner.

findings.fact: H7 is a legal discard on an unbeatable diamond lead.
findings.explanation: Authorized facts show West leading DJ, North holding only S8 and H7, and ten declarer tricks already won. Neither North card can win a diamond trick at notrump; retaining S8 is consistent with the conditional spade continuation.
quotes: Discard the heart, retaining spades for the final trick. Neither remaining card can beat the diamond jack.

findings.fact: H6 legally discards while preserving the higher partnership spade.
findings.explanation: The authorized trick is DJ–H7–D9, with South holding S9 and H6 and North retaining S8. South is void in diamonds, so H6 is legal; retaining S9 follows the plan’s conditional attempt to obtain a final spade trick without asserting it will win.
quotes: Discard the heart and retain the higher spade for the last trick. Ten tricks are already secured.
